observations.title: Expenditure Exceeded the Budgeted Amount
observations.observation: Review of system-generated Budget Variance Sheets showed that significant overspending was made under various expense heads. Overspending was observed across multiple years under heads including Office Staff Salaries, Building Repair & Maintenance, Livery Expenses, Direct Cost – AC Repair, and Educational Visits.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Budget variance shall be monitored for judicious use of funds allocated under all Heads of Expenses. System generated budget variance sheet be consulted to monitor variance of expense against budget allocation and discrepancy, if any, rectified.' 'Branch Purchase Committee and certain analytical reports in the Module e.g. Imprest Budget Variance Statement shall provide support to BH in this regard.' 'Monitoring of Opex (Imprest) variances of Branches shall be conducted at RO Finance on monthly basis.'
observations.audit_view: Branch management should review budget variances on a monthly basis and obtain prior approval for any anticipated overspending. RO Finance should strengthen monitoring controls.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Budget for Student Expenditure Remained Unutilized
observations.observation: As per Company policy, savings under the category of student expenses should be avoided. During review of Budget Variance Sheets, it was observed that budget for student expenditure remained un-utilized in certain heads across multiple financial years.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'There should be no saving of funds under the category of student expenses.' Branch management should plan student activities and expenditures proactively to ensure budgeted funds are utilized for student welfare.
observations.audit_view: Branch should plan extracurricular activities, educational visits, and student welfare programs to utilize the allocated budget for student benefit.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Accounting Procedure not Followed / Bank Payment Vouchers
observations.observation: Cheques were prepared and issued without printing bank payment vouchers. Vouchers were printed after making the transaction. In certain instances, JVs and BRs were also printed with delay. Additionally, bank payments were found booked through Journal Vouchers instead of Bank Payment Vouchers.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'All bank payments shall be made after obtaining approval from the Branch Head on Bank Payment Vouchers.' 'BA is responsible for recording all receipts, payments and relevant entries in the module on daily basis after obtaining approval from the BH.' Bank payments should be booked through Bank Payment Vouchers only.
observations.audit_view: Proper sequencing of voucher preparation and payment is essential for maintaining audit trail. All transactions must be recorded in real-time.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Purchase Committee not Properly Functioning
observations.observation: The Purchase Committee members were not actively participating in PC-related activities. Bills exceeding PKR 5,000 were not being verified by Purchase Committee members. Members were not reviewing RFQ/CSQ documents or providing guidance on vendor management.
observations.recommendation: As per policy, general functions of PCs include: advise for sourcing strategy; provide guidance for vendor management; review and advise whether proposed procurement actions are in accordance with the Manual; review that equal opportunity is provided to every genuine competitor; review and evaluate RFQ, CSQ and related documents submitted; review negotiated price, terms & conditions.
observations.audit_view: Active participation of Purchase Committee is critical for ensuring transparency and compliance in procurement. BH should ensure all PC members are briefed on their roles and responsibilities.
observations.typical_response: Noted. PMC members are strictly guided to follow the procedure.

observations.title: Withholding Tax Deposited with Delay
observations.observation: Tax withheld from suppliers/vendors was not deposited within seven days from the date of payment as required. Delays were observed in the ledger for Withholding Tax U/s 50(4). This creates a risk of exposure to penalties and interest charges by tax authorities.
observations.recommendation: As per SMFO-HO letter dated 04 Jul 2014: 'Please follow the instructions at your end and also instruct the schools and other concerned staff to deduct the tax accordingly and deposit the same into Government Treasury within seven days from the deduction and payment.' Branch Accountant must monitor tax deposit deadlines strictly.
observations.audit_view: Delayed deposit of withholding tax exposes the organization to statutory penalties. A compliance calendar should be maintained by the Branch Accountant.
observations.typical_response: Mentioned details belong to previous years. Currently we are strictly following the instructions and procedures.

observations.title: Reimbursements not Timely Processed by RO
observations.observation: Delays were observed in the processing of reimbursement claims by Regional Office. Several claims were not processed within the stipulated 20-day timeframe. This results in cash flow pressure on branches that have to incur expenses from limited imprest funds.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt. SMF-RO and Manager Accounts at HO shall ensure reconciliation of inter office reimbursements balances on monthly basis.'
observations.audit_view: RO Finance should prioritize timely processing of branch reimbursement claims. If the 20-day timeline is not practicable, it should be formally revised through the proper policy amendment procedure.
observations.typical_response: Some bills are based on purchase orders (POs) forwarded to relevant departments for PO generation, which can take time. In practical scenario 20 days' time is insufficient.

observations.title: Splitting of Transactions to Bypass Company Policies
observations.observation: Transactions were apparently split to avoid obtaining competitive quotations, preparing a comparative statement, and issuing a Purchase Order (PO). Examples: Soft Boards procured as two separate transactions on the same day; Conservance items purchased from same vendor in multiple transactions on same/consecutive days totaling Rs. 632,125; Tea items purchased from same vendor on consecutive days. Similar instances were noted where the requirement of obtaining multiple quotations (for tasks exceeding PKR 25,000) was circumvented by splitting the activity.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Breaking or splitting a transaction into smaller values to avoid approval from concerned authorities will be considered a violation of this policy.' 'Procurement of Opex items having value PKR 25,000 or above requires competitive bidding.' Branch management must ensure all procurement is conducted in a transparent and consolidated manner.
observations.audit_view: Transaction splitting is a serious control violation that undermines procurement transparency. Branch Head must ensure all purchases are planned in advance and consolidated to avoid policy circumvention. Repeated instances may warrant disciplinary action.
observations.typical_response: Noted. We will be more careful and vigilant in future.

observations.title: Procurement at Higher Rates than Market Rates
observations.observation: Staff of branch had made purchases at higher rates as compared to the market. Physical verification and market comparison confirmed overcharging by vendors for certain items including Track Lights and hardware items.
observations.recommendation: Procurement processes should be strengthened to ensure purchases are made at competitive market rates. Mandatory market comparison should be conducted before finalizing any purchase. Purchase Committee should actively review rates.
observations.audit_view: Overpayment to vendors results in financial loss to the organization. A robust price benchmarking mechanism and active Purchase Committee oversight can prevent such occurrences.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance. Guidance to the concerned OFA will be provided.

observations.title: Vendors Registration not Properly Performed
observations.observation: Procurement was being made from unregistered vendors. VRA (Vendor Registration Application) Forms and supporting documents were not available for many vendors. In one campus, no vendor registration had been conducted since the accountant's joining in September 2023.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'The procurement shall be made from registered vendors. The registered vendor is a vendor for which Vendor Master Data is created in Vendor Register for Branches based on approved VRF. BH shall review the documents submitted and provide approval on VRF for inclusion in Vendor Register, upon satisfaction.' Branch Head must review the vendor register at least once annually.
observations.audit_view: Procuring from unregistered vendors exposes the organization to financial and reputational risk. An immediate vendor registration drive should be conducted and future procurements restricted to registered vendors only.
observations.typical_response: Will complete the remaining regular vendor registration before follow-up visit.

observations.title: Periodic Evaluation of Registered Vendors not Performed
observations.observation: The practice of periodic evaluation of registered vendors was not being followed. Vendor Performance Evaluation Forms had not been completed by BPC members within the required two-year cycle.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'BH shall be responsible for the timely evaluation of vendors. Designated Official(s) of BPC shall perform the periodic evaluation of registered vendors, at least once in two years, by completing Vendor Performance Evaluation Form.'
observations.audit_view: Regular vendor evaluation ensures service quality and competitive pricing. BH must schedule and conduct vendor evaluations as per the prescribed timeline.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Incongruities in Preparation & Filing of Purchase Orders
observations.observation: POs/WOs were not pre-numbered and copies were not filed in sequential order. Vendor acceptance was not being properly obtained on Purchase Orders.
observations.recommendation: Purchase orders/work orders should be pre-numbered and sequentially filed once acknowledged by vendors. 'PO shall be handed over/forwarded to vendor, by the designated Official of SC/BA for vendor's acceptance.' Acknowledgement from vendor must be obtained and filed.
observations.audit_view: Proper PO management with sequential numbering and vendor acknowledgement is essential for contractual control and audit trail purposes.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Copy of Cheques not Properly Attached with Voucher
observations.observation: Photocopy of cheques were not being attached with Bank Payment Vouchers. Additionally, cheque numbers of certain transactions were not recorded in Bank Payment Vouchers, creating difficulties in bank reconciliation.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Photocopy of the cheque shall also be attached with the voucher.' Cheque number for each transaction should be recorded to facilitate bank reconciliation.
observations.audit_view: Maintaining complete documentation including cheque copies ensures a proper audit trail and facilitates reconciliation.
observations.typical_response: Noted. Now we are strictly following the instructions and procedures.

observations.title: Transactions not Routed Through Vendor Ledger
observations.observation: Payments to regular/major vendors were made without routing them through their respective vendor ledgers. This results in incomplete vendor-wise transaction history.
observations.recommendation: Branch should ensure that related transactions are properly routed through vendor ledgers. As per policy: 'In case of major/regular vendors, the entries shall be recorded in accordance with the prescribed procedure.'
observations.audit_view: Routing transactions through vendor ledgers enables proper balance confirmation, facilitates reconciliation, and strengthens internal controls.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Excess Amount Charged by Paint Contractor
observations.observation: Paint-work contractor claimed excessive measurements in bills. Physical measurement performed by S&A Team in presence of Branch OFA and Branch Assistant Accountant confirmed overcharging. The contractor overcharged Rs. 41,882 for paint-work executed in year 2024. Both Branch OFA and Branch Assistant Accountant acknowledged the discrepancy.
observations.recommendation: Excess amount of Rs. 41,882 charged by the Vendor should be recovered or adjusted from other bills of the vendor. Validated paint area measurements endorsed by RO Works Department should be maintained to prevent future overcharging.
observations.audit_view: The recovery/deduction of Rs. 41,882 needs to be made at the earliest from the vendor, with intimation to relevant personnel of Systems & Audit department. A joint measurement exercise with Works Department should be conducted and maintained on record.
observations.typical_response: Vendor contacted and he agreed to deduct the difference from his payment.

observations.title: Validated Paint Area Measurement not Available
observations.observation: Total paintable area of the premises was prepared by Branch Management but had not been endorsed/verified by RO Works Department. Without validated measurements, there is no independent basis to verify contractor bills.
observations.recommendation: Branch should maintain an updated record of paint area measurement duly endorsed by relevant personnel at RO Works Department. This should be used as the basis for verifying all paint contractor bills.
observations.audit_view: Without independently verified paint area measurements, branches are vulnerable to overcharging by contractors. A joint verification with Works Department is strongly recommended.
observations.typical_response: Will prepare the detail and get it verified from ROC.

observations.title: Cash in Hand Exceeded the Prescribed Limit
observations.observation: Closing balance of cash in hand had exceeded the prescribed limit of Rs. 25,000 on various occasions throughout the audit period. This creates risk of misappropriation and theft.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'The maximum limit of closing balance of cash in hand is PKR 25,000.' Excess cash should be deposited in the bank account immediately. Branch Accountant should monitor daily cash balance.
observations.audit_view: Maintaining cash balances above prescribed limits increases the risk of misappropriation. Excess cash must be deposited promptly.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Negative Balance of Bank Ledger
observations.observation: In certain instances, the balance of the bank ledger was negative (credit) at end of business day. This indicates either timing differences in recording, or issuance of cheques without availability of sufficient funds.
observations.recommendation: BA should ensure that all transactions are recorded in real-time and reconciled promptly to prevent discrepancies. 'BA is responsible for recording all receipts, payments and relevant entries in the module on daily basis.' Cheques should only be issued after confirming availability of funds.
observations.audit_view: Negative bank ledger balance is a serious accounting deficiency. Real-time recording and daily reconciliation are essential to maintain accurate financial records.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance. Strict monitoring will be maintained.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Cash Collection Activities
observations.observation: Record for cash collection activities was not properly maintained: No record before March 2023; company policies for obtaining quotations and preparing CSQ were not complied with; Class Lists from system and summary of cash collection were not attached; certain activities were open and details not properly appearing.
observations.recommendation: Class Teacher shall obtain a Class List from the system and record the amount received against each student name. CT shall submit amount collected along with CL to Coordinator within two days from last date in Circular. The Branch Accountant should submit the activity account at closure of the activity to the School Head for approval.
observations.audit_view: Proper record-keeping for cash collection activities is essential to ensure all collected amounts are accounted for and deposited correctly.
observations.typical_response: Mentioned details belong to previous years. Currently we are strictly following the instructions and procedures.

observations.title: Missing Approval for Blood Relatives in Same Branch
observations.observation: Some blood relatives/related family members were working in the same branch for which approval from Head of HR (HHR) was not available. Conflict of Interest Disclosure Forms were also not properly filed.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'No blood relations and related family members shall be hired in the same Office/Branch; any exception shall be provided by the HHR.' Conflict of Interest Disclosure Forms must be obtained and filed for all such cases.
observations.audit_view: Working of family members in the same branch without HHR approval violates HR policy and creates conflict of interest. All existing cases must be regularized immediately through proper approval channels.
observations.typical_response: Employees' conflict of interest disclosure forms have been made and sent to HR-ROC for approval.

observations.title: Delay in Employee Confirmations
observations.observation: Confirmation of certain employees was not made within the required timeframe after completion of the six-month probationary period. No intimation of extension of probation was provided to employees in several cases. Copy of extension letters were also not provided.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'All regular employees are required to complete an initial probationary period of six working months extendable for a period of three working months on grounds of performance issues supported by documented reasons.' BEAMS generates a system intimation email to line manager one month before end of probation. Confirmation orders must be issued timely.
observations.audit_view: Delayed confirmation of employees creates ambiguity regarding employee status and may lead to HR disputes. Timely issuance of confirmation/extension orders with proper communication is essential.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Outgoing/Departure Attendance not Marked by Staff
observations.observation: Outgoing/departure attendance was not marked by various staff members in multiple instances. This results in incomplete attendance records and makes it difficult to monitor actual working hours.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor attendance record. Staff should raise application for attendance not marked or early leaving. As per policy: 'Employees shall mark their attendance on biometric devices (online attendance) installed in offices.'
observations.audit_view: In cases of 'Employee Out' not marked, application for 'Attendance not Marked' should be raised. In cases of deliberate and habitual non-compliance, appropriate disciplinary action should be taken by HR.
observations.typical_response: We have strictly instructed all staff to follow the guidelines.

observations.title: Short Office Hours
observations.observation: Instances were observed in which employees had not complied with the prescribed timings and left early without submitting required applications. This was observed across teaching and non-teaching staff.
observations.recommendation: Employees should follow office hours as mentioned in BEAMS. Branch Head should actively monitor attendance records. In case of early departure, a Short Leave application must be submitted. In cases of deliberate and habitual non-compliance, appropriate action should be taken by the HR department.
observations.audit_view: Habitual early leaving without application constitutes a disciplinary matter. Branch Head should take corrective action and where necessary escalate to HR.
observations.typical_response: Noted.

observations.title: Delay in Final Settlement of Employees
observations.observation: Final settlement claims of left employees were finalized with significant delays beyond the stipulated three-week timeframe. Certain employee records were also found missing in settlement files.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Keeping in view all the requirements, the clearance and final settlement process must not take more than three working weeks barring exceptions.' 'Final settlement of employees shall be paid within 45 days of their last working days.' Missing records must be traced and attached.
observations.audit_view: RO office should expedite the final settlement process. Delays particularly during July–October are noted due to profit calculations and online cheque issuance timelines. If prescribed timelines are not practicable, they should be formally revised.
observations.typical_response: Delays persist during July to October due to profit calculations at Corporate Finance and online cheque issuance process.

observations.title: Incomplete Employee Files
observations.observation: Documents were missing in employee files including: Detailed CV, photographs, attested CNIC copy, nomination forms, health insurance forms, emergency contact information, signed undertakings, security clearance forms, and confirmation letters.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Files of all School employees shall be maintained and updated properly.' 'Branch Head shall ensure that all the required documents are filed in personal files of employees as per the checklist pasted in the file.'
observations.audit_view: Branch should ensure completeness of all employee files. Since audit was performed on sample basis, branch management should review all employee files comprehensively.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance. Completing mentioned documentation.

observations.title: Reference Check / Security Reference Check not in Practice
observations.observation: The Reference Check Form (HRM-008) and Security Reference Check Form (HRM-012) were not attached in any employee files selected for audit. These forms are prescribed in HR policy for all new hires.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'The concerned HR Department shall check the employment history and references of the final candidate(s) under consideration through a formal Employee Reference Check Form (HRM-008).' 'Concerned HR staff shall attach Security Reference Check Form (HRM-012) in the personnel file of a new employee.'
observations.audit_view: Compliance with employee reference and security check procedures is essential, especially given the nature of work involving children. If forms need to be updated, the change should be referred to concerned authorities.
observations.typical_response: The form is not currently implemented in schools. Discussions are underway.

observations.title: EOBI Numbers not Updated in BEAMS
observations.observation: EOBI numbers of some employees were not updated in BEAMS Basic Info Report. Additionally, certain employees were not registered with EOBI at all. PESSI/SESSI records including copy of data forms/cards of relevant staff were also not available in branch.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'BA shall make necessary arrangement for registration of employees who are not registered with EOBI.' EOBI registration should be made immediately upon joining of employee and updated in module. Proper procedure should be devised for PESSI/SESSI registration, record-keeping, and monthly payments.
observations.audit_view: EOBI and social security compliance is a statutory requirement. Non-compliance may expose the organization to legal liability. A comprehensive review of all employee registrations is recommended.
observations.typical_response: All employees are registered in EOBI; only EOBI numbers are not updated on BEAMS — will be updated soon.

observations.title: Social Security Cards not Filed / Numbers not Updated
observations.observation: Copy of Social Security Cards were not filed in respective personal files. Social Security Card Numbers had not been updated in BEAMS by the Branch Accountant.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'BA shall obtain copy of Social Security Cards from employees and file these in respective personal files.' 'The BA shall obtain the Social Security Number from employees and update the same in BEAMS.'
observations.audit_view: Complete social security record is essential for regulatory compliance and employee benefit management.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Reports in BEAMS not Matched
observations.observation: Discrepancy was observed between employee count in different BEAMS reports. The number of employees in the branch listing did not match the Basic Info Report, with a difference of 7 employees. Left employees were still appearing in system due to incomplete data entry.
observations.recommendation: Branch management should review reports and coordinate with HR Department for earliest resolution. Left employees' data must be updated in BEAMS with correct leaving dates.
observations.audit_view: Data integrity in BEAMS is critical for payroll accuracy and HR compliance. Regular reconciliation of BEAMS reports should be conducted.
observations.typical_response: Some left employees are still showing due to leave date not entered by HR-ROC. Email sent to HR-ROC.

observations.title: Handing/Taking Over Procedure not Followed
observations.observation: Formal HOTO (Handing Over/Taking Over) procedure was not followed in multiple cases for Branch Heads and PROs. Approved copy of HOTO documents were not available in branches. Audit observations HOTO (HRM-031) was also not obtained.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'The overall responsibility of smooth and effective HOTO task rests with the BH/FI/HOD of the departing employee.' 'S&A Official(s) shall discuss unresolved points of Audit Report(s) with departing BH/BA and obtain HOTO of Audit Observations (HRM-031) from joining employee for their resolution.'
observations.audit_view: Proper HOTO ensures continuity of operations and accountability for outstanding items. RO should enforce HOTO compliance and forward approved copies to branches.
observations.typical_response: Referred to Regional Office.

observations.title: Employee Registration on Biometric Device with Delay
observations.observation: Employees hired were registered with delay on Biometric Device beyond the prescribed two-day timeframe after joining.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Employees must get themselves registered on one or more biometric devices within two days of their joining.' Registration on biometric devices and updating of timing schedule shall be performed as per the responsibilities matrix.
observations.audit_view: Delayed biometric registration results in incomplete attendance records for new employees. This should be treated as a priority task on the employee's first day.
observations.typical_response: Due to late submission of documents the employee was registered late.

observations.title: Leave Applications not Raised on BEAMS
observations.observation: Employees did not raise leave applications on BEAMS in multiple cases, resulting in absent deductions from salary instead of proper leave balances being utilized.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'All employees are required to inform their LM/HOD in advance or at the latest within the initial hours of the day in question if they need to take Casual or Medical Leave. Upon resuming duty, employees shall submit their leave application through BEAMS to their approving authority.'
observations.audit_view: Branch staff should be instructed to raise timely leave applications on BEAMS to ensure accurate leave and payroll records.
observations.typical_response: Informed to employees and noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Outstation Claimed for Personal Works
observations.observation: Some employees had apparently forwarded applications for 'Outstation' against their personal works, and such applications were approved. In one case, no reason was mentioned but the application was approved.
observations.recommendation: 'Outstation' should only be applied for official visits or meetings at a place other than the employee's work premises. Proper reason must be mentioned. As per policy: 'Employees going on an official outstation visit must submit an application at least one day before or within three working days after completion of outstation visit.'
observations.audit_view: Since these instances were identified on a sample basis, Branch Management should review the complete record and coordinate with HR. Approving authorities must scrutinize outstation applications carefully.
observations.typical_response: Mentioned details belong to previous years. Currently strictly following instructions.

observations.title: Delay in Providing Livery Items
observations.observation: Delays in providing livery items to entitled employees were observed. Livery record prior to a certain period was also not available in the branch.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'The activity to procure livery shall be initiated considering provision of summer uniform in April and winter uniform in September.' Livery shall be provided to regular/contractual entitled employees in accordance with their entitlement. Record of livery issued must be maintained.
observations.audit_view: Timely procurement of livery items requires advance planning. Procurement must be initiated well before the April/September deadlines.
observations.typical_response: Livery orders were placed on time, but vendor provided them late.

observations.title: Salary Paid Through Branch Bank Account
observations.observation: Salary-related transactions were being made from the Branch Bank Account/Imprest instead of through the designated salary payment channel. Salary reimbursements were later claimed from RO.
observations.recommendation: Salary of all employees should be processed through the designated salary payment procedure adopted by the organization. Direct salary payment from branch bank account is not permitted.
observations.audit_view: Processing salary from branch imprest creates accounting complications and bypasses payroll controls. Designated salary bank accounts must be used for all salary payments.
observations.typical_response: We are currently following the policy. Previous practice has been changed.

observations.title: Early Confirmation of Employee without Approval
observations.observation: An employee was confirmed early without completion of probationary period and without approval from Head HR.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'All regular employees are required to complete an initial probationary period of six working months.' 'If a confirmed employee is re-hired, before the completion of six months the appointing authority may employ him/her as a confirmed employee after approval of Head HR.' Relevant approval must be placed in employee file.
observations.audit_view: Branch management is requested to attach relevant approval in employee file and ensure such early confirmations only occur with requisite HHR approval.
observations.typical_response: Noted. Mentioned detail belongs to previous years.

observations.title: Sandwich Leaves not Considered
observations.observation: As per BSS policies, gazetted/official leaves sandwiched between employees' leaves should be counted as part of leaves. In a few instances, sandwich leaves were not accounted for correctly.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Off days or gazetted holidays falling in between leave periods (sandwiched) shall be counted as part of that leave.' Leaves not auto-dealt by the system should be reported to RO-HR for manual adjustment.
observations.audit_view: The leaves which are not auto-dealt by BEAMS should be reported to RO-HR to account for as per policy.
observations.typical_response: These leaves are auto-adjusted by BEAMS.

observations.title: Registration Fee Deposited with Delay
observations.observation: There were delays in depositing the registration amount into the bank account beyond the prescribed weekly deadline. In some cases, amounts exceeding Rs. 10,000 were not deposited immediately as required.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Cash collected as registration fee shall be deposited in the main bank account designated for collection, by close of every working week. However, in cases where the collection exceeds PKR 10,000/- the same must be deposited immediately.' Cash collected on account of student registration shall not be utilized by the Branch under any circumstances.
observations.audit_view: Delayed deposit of registration fee increases the risk of misappropriation. PRO must hand over collected amounts to accountant on the same day of collection.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Incomplete / Wrong Student Information in BEAMS
observations.observation: Multiple data discrepancies observed in BEAMS: Father occupation not mentioned; Mother CNIC missing; Mother occupation left blank; City name not mentioned; Wrong gender of student; Missing contact information (phone numbers, addresses).
observations.recommendation: Concerned personnel should ensure complete and correct information is updated in BEAMS at the time of admission. PRO and BA are jointly responsible for accuracy of student data in the Integrated Student Module (ISM).
observations.audit_view: Complete and accurate student data is essential for emergency contact purposes and regulatory compliance. Branch should ensure completeness of all student data as audit was performed on sample basis.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Incomplete Student Files
observations.observation: Documents such as copy of parent's CNIC, birth certificates, photographs, and registration/admission forms were missing in student files. Checklists were not properly attached and filled. Transfer orders were not properly attached in Transfer-in Student Files.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'It is the responsibility of the PRO to prepare the file for each student upon finalisation of the student admission process.' 'A detailed Student File Check List shall be pasted on the inside of the file cover. The PRO shall ensure that all required documents are filed in personal files of students.'
observations.audit_view: Branch should ensure completeness of all student files. Since audit was performed on sample basis, a comprehensive review of all student files is recommended.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance. Will coordinate with parents to update files.

observations.title: Files of Transferred-In Students not Available
observations.observation: Files of transferred-in students were not available in the branch. Turnaround time for file dispatch is prescribed as 1 week but was not being complied with.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'PRO of transferor Branch shall ensure the completeness of student file before its dispatch. The PRO of transferee Branch shall also ensure the same.' Turnaround time is 1 week. Contact transferor branch to locate missing files.
observations.audit_view: Although duplicate files have been prepared, the original missing files should be located and safe custody ensured. It is suggested to contact the transferor branch for file recovery.
observations.typical_response: Duplicate files have been made.

observations.title: Anomalies in Registration Fee Collection and Deposit
observations.observation: Multiple anomalies identified: Short deposit of Rs. 8,100 between registration amounts in BEAMS and available deposit slips; missing deposit slips; wrong deposit dates in BEAMS not matching actual bank deposit slips; deposit dates earlier than receipt dates; wrong deposit slip numbers in BEAMS.
observations.recommendation: Registration fee should be deposited in full and within stipulated time. Correct dates and slip numbers must be recorded in BEAMS. BH must validate bank deposit slips and registration receipts. Parent signatures must be obtained on receipts.
observations.audit_view: Short deposit and date discrepancies are serious control weaknesses that require immediate investigation. All discrepancies should be reconciled and shortfall recovered.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Registration Fee Collected Without Issuing Receipt
observations.observation: Registration receipts were recorded on Saturday and Sunday (non-working days), indicating registration fee was collected without issuing a receipt to parents. Student registrations were later entered into the system on non-working days. Manual registration receipts were also not provided.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Registration Fee shall be collected in cash and Registration Fee Acknowledgement Receipt shall be issued to Parents/Students as acknowledgement of cash received.' 'In case of non-availability of BEAMS Process Manager, Registration Fee Acknowledgement Receipt shall be issued as acknowledgement.' 'MRR must be printed, pre-numbered and issued in order.'
observations.audit_view: Collection of fees without issuance of receipts is a fundamental control weakness. All collections must be immediately receipted to protect both the organization and the parents.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Fee Concession Approvals not Properly Filed
observations.observation: Approvals of fee concessions being availed by students were not properly attached in student files. Fee Exemption/Concession Forms were not verified by Regional Accountant/Senior Manager Finance-ROS in several cases.
observations.recommendation: Such approvals should be placed in respective student files. 'Fee exemption/Concession Form shall be submitted to RO for verification. Employee confirmation letter/Child birth certificate issued by NADRA shall be attached as supporting document.' PRO should check all files and attach relevant approvals.
observations.audit_view: Unauthorized fee concessions represent a financial risk. All concession approvals must be properly documented, verified by RO, and filed in student records.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Unclaimed Student Security
observations.observation: In certain cases, student security was appearing as 'Unclaimed Security' in BEAMS. Refund cheques were dispatched but not received by parents due to address issues and are now time-barred.
observations.recommendation: Student security should be refunded on a timely basis. As per policy: 'The cheque shall be dispatched through courier to the address provided on the forms by the parent/guardian.' A report/option in ISM/BEAMS should be available to PROs for monitoring security refund status.
observations.audit_view: It is requested to coordinate with IT for generating a branch-wise security refund report in BEAMS to enable more efficient tracking by branch PROs.
observations.typical_response: These are cases where refund was dispatched but not received and are now time-barred.

observations.title: Registration Receipts for Exempt/Reduced Fee Students not Issued
observations.observation: Registration receipts of students exempt from registration fee were not available. The practice of printing such receipts was not being followed.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Registration Receipt (RR) shall also be issued to students who are exempted from registration fee e.g. employee children, pre-mature transfers. Such receipts shall be marked as Exempted along with the reason/basis.'
observations.audit_view: Issuing receipts even for exempted students creates a proper audit trail and prevents disputes.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Untraced Fixed Assets
observations.observation: Assets appearing in the Fixed Assets Register could not be physically located by the concerned staff. Status regarding untraced assets from previous audit instances was also pending resolution.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Principals/Branch Heads have the prime responsibility for the safe custody of the assets of the Company.' All untraced assets must be thoroughly investigated. AMCO and RO Fixed Assets department should be involved for resolution.
observations.audit_view: Concerned AMCO and RO Fixed Assets department is requested to look into the matter and resolve the issue at the earliest. Yearly stock take activity should include a comprehensive check of all previously untraced assets.
observations.typical_response: Already disposed off. Will trace and update.

observations.title: Out of Order Assets
observations.observation: During physical verification, several assets were found out of order, broken, or non-functional. No action (repair or disposal through AIDN) had been initiated for many such assets.
observations.recommendation: Out of order/repairable assets should be repaired at the earliest. Assets beyond repair should be processed for disposal as per policy: 'Assets are sold when: Assets are beyond repair or where the cost of repair is considerably high; Assets are obsolete; Company for any other reason has no use of the assets.' AIDN should be processed without delay.
observations.audit_view: Maintaining out-of-order assets without action is a waste of resources and affects the branch's operational efficiency. A comprehensive audit of asset condition should be conducted and appropriate action taken promptly.
observations.typical_response: Will initiate AIDN for disposal/repair in coordination with RO.

observations.title: Unmatched Assets Found in Branch
observations.observation: Some assets were physically present in the branch but were not appearing in the Fixed Assets Register. Source of receipt for these assets could not be determined.
observations.recommendation: The source from which these assets were received should be traced with the consultation of RO, and the fixed assets register should be updated accordingly. 'Fixed assets without codes or having unmatched codes shall not be transferred.'
observations.audit_view: Unmatched assets indicate control gaps in asset management. RO Fixed Assets department must be involved to update the register and assign proper codes.
observations.typical_response: Noted and will be rectified.

observations.title: Un-Numbered Assets
observations.observation: Some assets were found without fixed asset codes/numbers during physical verification. This makes it impossible to track assets and match them to the register.
observations.recommendation: Asset numbers should be affixed immediately. If numbers have not been received, GRNs should be checked and RO coordinated with. As per policy: 'Fixed assets shall affix codes on respective fixed assets within 15 days of receipt of fixed assets codes.'
observations.audit_view: Un-numbered assets cannot be effectively tracked or controlled. An urgent exercise to number all un-numbered assets should be conducted.
observations.typical_response: Noted and will be rectified.

observations.title: Duplicate / Same Codes on Two Assets
observations.observation: Some assets were observed with duplicate/same fixed asset codes affixed to more than one asset. This creates confusion in the register and physical verification process.
observations.recommendation: As per policy, unique codes should be assigned and affixed within 15 days of receipt. Duplicate codes must be investigated and corrected immediately by coordinating with RO Fixed Assets department.
observations.audit_view: Duplicate asset codes undermine the integrity of the fixed assets register. An immediate reconciliation with RO is required.
observations.typical_response: Activity still in process. Will be updated soon.

observations.title: Physical Verification Report not Available
observations.observation: Physical verification reports for fixed assets were not available in the branch. Annual physical verification as required by policy had not been conducted/documented.
observations.recommendation: The stock take reports should be retrieved for future reference. As per policy: 'Physical verification of all fixed assets (100%) shall be conducted at least once in a year.'
observations.audit_view: Annual physical verification is a fundamental internal control. Branch must ensure this is conducted and documented every year.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Fixed Asset Register — Missing Aspects and Columns
observations.observation: Only the category of assets was mentioned, but aspects containing description (Brand, Make, Model) were not available in the fixed asset register. Certain columns were left blank including GRN number, supplier name, invoice number, and PO reference.
observations.recommendation: In order to physically verify assets authentically, Brand, Make, Model, and other identifying information must be included in the FA Register. Complete information should be entered for all assets. This is now being addressed through the Oracle-based fixed assets dashboard.
observations.audit_view: Incomplete FA Register makes physical verification unreliable. In recent years, aspects of assets have been included following development of Oracle-based dashboard — this practice must be applied to all assets.
observations.typical_response: Referred to Regional Office.

observations.title: List of Landlord/Canteen/Photocopier Assets not Available
observations.observation: Detailed list of landlord/canteen contractor/photocopier assets in the branch premises was not available or not updated. Lists were not signed and verified by both parties.
observations.recommendation: Detail of landlord/contractor assets, duly signed by both parties, should be kept in the branch to differentiate the assets of the company from assets of the landlord/contractor. Lists should be updated whenever assets change.
observations.audit_view: Without a verified list of third-party assets, there is risk of company assets being removed or third-party assets being included in company records.
observations.typical_response: Will coordinate with ROC to identify. Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Assets Disposed Off but Still in FAR / Physically Present
observations.observation: Certain assets were disposed off against formal AIDN but were still appearing in the Fixed Assets Register. Additionally, some disposed assets were physically still present in the branch.
observations.recommendation: Assets disposed off should be removed from the Branch's FAR and should not be physically present in the branch after disposal. An immediate reconciliation of disposed assets with current FAR is required.
observations.audit_view: Discrepancy between disposal records and FAR/physical presence indicates control failure in asset disposal process. A comprehensive reconciliation must be conducted.
observations.typical_response: These assets have now been removed from the updated FAR.

observations.title: High Item Per Child Book Ratio in Library
observations.observation: Books per child ratio exceeded the prescribed standard of approximately 15 books per child. Ratios of 26.75 and 31.60 were observed against the standard of 15.
observations.recommendation: As per Library Manual clause 18.1: 'A school librarian should always be aware of her library material, student strength and items per child.' RO Librarian should monitor item per child ratios across all branches and facilitate transfer or disposal of excess books.
observations.audit_view: Excess books should be discussed with RO Librarian before any disposal decision. Excess books may be transferred to branches with lower IPC ratios or stored as per direction of RO.
observations.typical_response: We will discard old books.

observations.title: Low Item Per Child Ratio in Library
observations.observation: Book ratio per child was low in middle section library. As per the item per child report of June 30, 2025, only 4.53 books per student (middle) were available against the standard of 15 books per child.
observations.recommendation: As per Library Manual clause 18.1: 'A school librarian should always be aware of her library material, student strength and items per child.' Additional books should be procured as per budget to meet the prescribed ratio.
observations.audit_view: Low IPC ratio impacts the reading culture and educational experience. Budget planning for library books must be prioritized.
observations.typical_response: Will purchase books accordingly with budget in this session.

observations.title: Delay in Return of Library Books
observations.observation: Library books were not returned within the stipulated time by students and teachers. Books overdue exceeding 25 days and 100 days were identified. Outstanding books appearing on KOHA system not returned by students.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'A library book may be issued for a maximum period of two weeks at a time. Renewals may be permitted based on availability.' KOHA should be regularly monitored for overdue items. Reminders should be sent and follow-up calls made to parents.
observations.audit_view: A systematic reminder mechanism through KOHA should be implemented. Habitual non-return should be escalated to Branch Head.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance. Now data has been updated.

observations.title: Books not Entered in Library Module KOHA
observations.observation: Around 150-600 books were not yet entered in the Library Module KOHA. In one branch, the librarian stated these books would be disposed off without being recorded.
observations.recommendation: Entry of library books in module should be completed for all books. All books should be accessible in the module on timely basis. Books below 1000 should be recorded in the relevant register instead of Main Accession Register.
observations.audit_view: Proper cataloguing of all books in KOHA is essential for effective library management and accurate IPC calculation.
observations.typical_response: Books were added to KOHA but physical labelling had not yet been completed.

observations.title: Incomplete Barcode Labelling on Library Books
observations.observation: Barcode labels were not affixed on many library books. Barcode printer issues and worn-out plastic covers contributed to the problem.
observations.recommendation: Bar Codes (KOHA) should be pasted on all books on timely basis. As per email from Deputy Manager Libraries-South Nov 2018: 'KOHA will be implemented in all branches.' All books must have barcode labels before being placed on shelves.
observations.audit_view: Branch should ensure completeness of barcode labelling on all books. Since audit was performed on sample basis, a comprehensive review of all books is recommended.
observations.typical_response: Measures are being taken to resolve printer issues and re-labelling is in progress.

observations.title: Library Books in Poor Condition / Torn Pages
observations.observation: Few library books were in bad condition with torn covers, torn-out pages, or missing titles. Books without plastic covers were deteriorating faster.
observations.recommendation: As per Library Manual Clause 8.1: 'To maintain efficient running of the school library, constant maintaining of resources should be an on-going procedure. Books should be mended, repaired, bound and re-bound so that they are maintained in a fit condition.' Books in very poor condition should be withdrawn from circulation and either repaired or disposed of.
observations.audit_view: Regular book maintenance and plastic coating is essential for preserving library resources. An annual book condition audit should be conducted.
observations.typical_response: Regular inspection and repair of books have been part of ongoing library practices.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Cost of Books / Wrong Data in KOHA
observations.observation: Books with the same title were recorded at significantly different costs in the Main Accession Register. Zero cost and incomplete data were appearing for books in KOHA. Certain columns were left blank or contained incorrect data.
observations.recommendation: Correct cost should be recorded for all books. Complete and correct information must be maintained in all library records. Branch Librarian must verify and correct all data discrepancies.
observations.audit_view: Accurate data in KOHA is fundamental for effective library management and valuation. A comprehensive data cleansing exercise should be undertaken.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance. Data correction task has been started.

observations.title: Transfer and Disposal of Books not Processed in KOHA
observations.observation: Books were physically transferred from the branch but were not recorded in the accession register even after lapse of five years. Disposal of books was not properly processed in KOHA with certain AIDNs pending.
observations.recommendation: Transfer notes and disposal processes should be completed within a reasonable time to ensure correct records and accurate IPC calculation.
observations.audit_view: Pending transfers and disposals distort the actual book count and IPC ratio. Immediate processing of all pending transactions is required.
observations.typical_response: Noted and task is in process.

observations.title: Double Stacking of Books in Library
observations.observation: Books were double stacked in the library. As per standard practice, double stacking should be avoided for proper display and easy access to books.
observations.recommendation: Proper stacking should be done as per policy and standard library practice. Books should be organized for maximum visibility and accessibility.
observations.audit_view: Double stacking makes it difficult to locate books and may damage them. Additional shelving or book reduction/transfer should be considered.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Library Record not Properly Maintained
observations.observation: Certain library records were not properly maintained: Minutes of Library Coordination Meeting not filed; Reminders file for overdue books not maintained; Library Clearance Forms not properly kept on record; File for minutes of librarian meeting with regional librarian not maintained.
observations.recommendation: As per Library Manual: 'Minutes of the Library Coordination Meeting should be filed by the librarian. A file should be maintained with a copy of Reminders issued to teachers/students for not returning books on time. Library Clearance forms should be kept on record properly.' Regional Librarian should call meetings at least once/twice per academic year.
observations.audit_view: Proper documentation of library activities ensures accountability and effective monitoring.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Guards Strength Approved Copy not Available
observations.observation: Detail of approved quantity of security guards was not available in the branch. The SLA shared with branches did not mention the number of guards.
observations.recommendation: RO should communicate/intimate the branches regarding the approved/allowed number of security personnel in writing. Number of guards authorized as per approved OPEX sheet should be formally communicated.
observations.audit_view: Branch management should have documented approval for guard strength to ensure proper security coverage and cost control.
observations.typical_response: Email available in branch. Number of guards are authorized as per approved OPEX sheet.

observations.title: Discrepancies in School Security
observations.observation: Several security deficiencies identified: Visitor entries not properly recorded (CNIC, phone, signature, purpose missing); Perimeter wall not complying with minimum height of 8'+2' in certain areas; Trees and construction along perimeter wall create security vulnerabilities; Barbed wire only 1.5 feet in some areas instead of required 2 feet and was rusted; Staff not wearing employee ID cards; Common boundary walls of adjacent vacant plot were soft areas; Glass doors without grills in important areas; Walk-through gate and checking staff in close proximity leaving no reaction time.
observations.recommendation: School management should seek guidance from RO Security Department to address all identified deficiencies. Visitor entries must be complete and signed. Perimeter security must meet minimum standards.
observations.audit_view: Security deficiencies must be addressed as a priority given the school environment. A formal security audit by RO Security Department is recommended.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: CCTV Recording Gaps
observations.observation: CCTV camera recordings were missing on different dates and timings due to old CCTV cables causing cameras to go offline.
observations.recommendation: Branch should ensure uninterrupted backup of CCTV recordings. Old cables and faulty equipment should be replaced immediately. A proper maintenance schedule for CCTV equipment should be established.
observations.audit_view: Gaps in CCTV recordings compromise school security. Immediate rectification of cable/equipment issues is essential.
observations.typical_response: Due to old CCTV cables the cameras were off.

observations.title: Annual Firing Practice not Conducted Regularly
observations.observation: First annual firing practice was conducted in 2019 followed by last practice in 2023 — a gap of more than four years without firing practice.
observations.recommendation: Regional annual firing practice should be conducted at the firing range at least once per year. As per Pistol Handling SOPs: 'At least one time fire is necessary in a year.' Official records must be maintained.
observations.audit_view: Regular firing practice is essential to maintain readiness and proficiency of armed security personnel. RO Security Department should ensure annual practice is conducted and recorded.
observations.typical_response: Security Department will work on obtaining additional ammunition for annual firing practice.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Security Guard Documentation
observations.observation: Multiple security guard documentation issues: Guards not within agreed age limit of 35-50 years as per contract; crucial documents of guards not available; security supervisor signing attendance on behalf of guards; guards possibly not adequately literate.
observations.recommendation: As per contract clause #4(b): 'Security guards will be preferably in the age group of 35-50 years.' All security guards should sign their own attendance sheets. Documentation of security guards must be accurate and complete. As per contract: 'Contractor will ensure that the deployed security guards are adequately educated.'
observations.audit_view: Contract compliance must be enforced with the security company. RO Security should verify guard documentation during routine checks.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Weapon/Ammunition Register
observations.observation: Weapon In/Out register was not signed by SGSM/RSM on visits. Weekly weapon cleaning log book was also not signed by SGSM/RSM.
observations.recommendation: As per Pistol Handling SOPs: 'After duty timings, the weapon and its ammunition shall be placed in lock and key, and timing of in and out will be entered in the register.' 'This register will be presented to RSM Security/SGSM on every visit for counter sign.'
observations.audit_view: Proper weapon register maintenance and supervisory sign-off is essential for accountability and security compliance.
observations.typical_response: The relevant documents are being signed by Managers Security during their routine duties.

observations.title: UPS not Available / Control Room Security Deficiencies
observations.observation: Control Room/Security Room was shared with OFA, making it a frequently visited area and compromising security of critical operations. The CCTV system was not automatically connected to UPS backup, requiring manual intervention during power outages.
observations.recommendation: Security Control Room should not be shared with general staff. It should be furnished with automatic UPS backup for uninterrupted surveillance. A separate UPS for CCTV/control room equipment should be provided.
observations.audit_view: An unsecured and shared control room with unreliable power backup represents a serious security vulnerability. Immediate corrective measures are required.
observations.typical_response: OFA office shifting is under process. Will demand separate UPS in upcoming CAPEX.

observations.title: Security Guards Frequently Changed by Security Company
observations.observation: Security guards were frequently changed by the security company, making it difficult for the branch to remain familiar with the guards and creating security vulnerabilities.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Ensure that security companies providing security guards maintain a separate pool of guards for BSS and do not change them frequently/at will.' Non-compliance should be escalated to RO Security.
observations.audit_view: Frequent guard changes undermine security by ensuring guards are unfamiliar with the premises and staff. Contract enforcement through RO Security is required.
observations.typical_response: Requested security company to change incompetent guards.

observations.title: Ex-Armed Forces Personnel not Provided as per Contract
observations.observation: None of the 6 armed guards of the school had ex-armed forces background, while the Security Company contract requires 50% ex-armed forces personnel.
observations.recommendation: As per the contract: 'Security Company has to provide 50% ex-armed forces personnel.' The non-compliance of the security services contract should be reported to the concerned office and followed up until the issue is resolved.
observations.audit_view: Failure to provide ex-armed forces personnel as contractually required is a material breach of contract. RO should formally notify the security company and enforce compliance.
observations.typical_response: Noted for compliance.

observations.title: Assembly Area Not Properly Marked
observations.observation: Assembly area label was present in branch. However, designated assembly areas for specific groups (Primary Section, Middle Section, Senior Section, etc.) were not marked.
observations.recommendation: Assembly area should be clearly labelled and sectioned as per the emergency plan of the branch to ensure smooth and organized evacuation during emergencies.
observations.audit_view: Clearly marked section-specific assembly areas are critical for effective emergency response, especially in a school setting with students of different age groups.
observations.typical_response: Necessary steps will be taken in future.

observations.title: No Scanning Room at Entry Gate
observations.observation: There was no scanning room available at Gate No. 3, while a number of visitors, parents and students entered the branch from this gate. A walkthrough gate was installed and operational but no dedicated scanning room was available.
observations.recommendation: Scanning Room should be available at each entry point for visitors to ensure thorough security checks.
observations.audit_view: A dedicated scanning room at all entry points is essential for maintaining school security standards. RO civil team should be engaged for layout and budgeting.
observations.typical_response: Will discuss with RO civil team to arrange required budgeting for execution.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Memorandum Registers
observations.observation: Various stock register discrepancies observed: Registers not maintained for required categories (Music Equipment, Fixed Assets below threshold, Sports, Teaching Aid, Consumable Stationery); Closing balances calculated incorrectly; Receipts recorded in issued column; Register not validated by Branch Head; Physical stock not matched with records.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'For the purpose of effective control, certain stock registers shall be maintained by Branches.' All registers must be properly maintained with correct entries, closing balances, and monthly BH validation. Old Stock Registers for last 6 years shall be kept safe.
observations.audit_view: Properly maintained stock registers are essential for accountability and control over low-value items. Branch Head must verify and sign registers on a monthly basis.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Document Tracking Sheet not in Practice
observations.observation: The branch was not in the practice of attaching the Document Tracking Sheet with documents being forwarded to different departments. This makes it difficult to track document movement and ensure timely delivery.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'DOCUMENT TRACKING SHEET shall be used on top of every such document(s) which involves movement within different organizational tiers or departments.' Important documents include GRNs, Transfer Notes, AIDNs for fixed assets, Final Settlement cases, and Reimbursement claims.
observations.audit_view: Document tracking sheets ensure accountability for document movement and help prevent loss of important records.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Generator Log Book not Properly Maintained
observations.observation: Generator log book was not properly maintained: Usage detail not properly updated; person making ON/OFF entry not signing; No proper record in logbooks before Sep 2023; Maintenance not recorded in Logbook; Repairs/Out of order of Generator not recorded. Fuel average monitoring was also not conducted.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'OFA/AO shall maintain the record (logbook & invoices) pertinent to generator operations including fueling.' The following information shall be recorded daily: Date & time of diesel re-filling; Quantity of fuel filled; Meter readings; Running hours; Fuel average; Replacement of parts; Detail of other maintenance activities.
observations.audit_view: A properly maintained generator logbook is essential for monitoring fuel consumption, maintenance compliance, and equipment longevity.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Demolition Register not Maintained
observations.observation: Demolition register was not being maintained at the branch.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'A demolition register shall be maintained at the Branch by the Officer Facility Administration or designated person, and should be vetted by the BH and designated Official of Construction/Works department RO.'
observations.audit_view: Demolition register is important for tracking any demolition/construction work at the branch premises.
observations.typical_response: Will be properly maintained and verified from ROC concerned officials.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Daycare Facility
observations.observation: Multiple daycare facility deficiencies: Daycare enrollment forms not available; CCTV camera blind spots in daycare; No telephone extension; No warning device for fire alarm; No smoke detector; No fire extinguisher; No first-aid kit; No refrigerator; Space for infants and children of other ages not separated.
observations.recommendation: As per Daycare Policy: Parents must complete enrollment forms; CCTV must cover daycare completely; daycare must have a telephone extension; early warning device for fire alarm must be provided; operable smoke detector must be placed in daycare room; fire extinguisher must be intact and accessible; first-aid kit must be available; clean refrigerator must be provided; space for infants must be separate from spaces for children of other ages.
observations.audit_view: Daycare facility deficiencies pose significant safety and liability risks. All non-compliant items must be addressed immediately as these relate directly to child safety.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Inward Gate Pass not in Practice
observations.observation: The practice of preparing inward gate passes for assets/items received was not implemented. This reduces visibility over inward movement of assets and items.
observations.recommendation: Gate pass system should be implemented for both inward and outward movements to ensure efficient monitoring and provide evidence of receipt of assets. Gate passes should be authorized, sequential, and properly documented.
observations.audit_view: A gate pass system provides essential control over asset movement. Both inward and outward movements must be documented with authorized gate passes.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Renewed School Business Registration Not Available
observations.observation: School Business Registration had expired on 09/07/2022 and the renewed certificate was not available. This exposes the school to regulatory non-compliance.
observations.recommendation: Registration of Education & Literacy Department should be renewed on a timely basis. RO Admin should provide a copy of the renewed school registration certificate to the branch.
observations.audit_view: Operating without a valid school business registration is a regulatory violation. Immediate renewal and provision of certificate to branch is required.
observations.typical_response: Noted for compliance.

observations.title: Printed Stationery Register not Maintained
observations.observation: Printed stationery register was not maintained. Quarterly verification and signing by Branch Head was not being done.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Printed Stationery register shall be checked and signed by the Branch Head, quarterly.' The officer authorized by BH shall be responsible for checking receipt and issuance of printed stationery stock against acknowledgement.
observations.audit_view: Printed stationery register is a control over pre-printed documents. Its absence creates risk of unauthorized use of official stationery.
observations.typical_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Chart of Account Needs Correction
observations.observation: Sub accounts were opened in inappropriate parent category of 'Advance to Suppliers'. Accountants at branch level only have rights to open accounts in certain categories, creating structural issues in the COA.
observations.recommendation: To present a fair view of accounts, the concerned heads should be revised and transferred to related parent head categories. RO Finance should consult HO Finance/IT for resolution of the system constraint.
observations.audit_view: RO Finance department should consult HO Finance/IT department for the resolution of the system constraint that forces incorrect account creation.
observations.typical_response: Accountants at branch level only have rights to open accounts in Advance to Supplier, Banks and Advance to Staff.

observations.title: Science Laboratory Stock Register Discrepancies
observations.observation: Laboratory stock registers were not validated by Branch Head; stock was not kept systematically with items from one lab kept in another; physical stock did not match with records; actual consumption not recorded on actual basis (stocktake on intervals with difference posted as consumption).
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'Branch Head shall verify the laboratory registers on monthly basis.' Physical balance should be matched with records. Consumption should be recorded on actual basis.
observations.audit_view: Discrepancies in laboratory stock registers indicate poor asset management in laboratories. Monthly BH validation is mandatory.
observations.typical_response: Laboratory In-charges have been instructed to maintain records regularly. BH will now validate and sign registers monthly.

observations.title: Track Record of Quotations not Maintained
observations.observation: For procurements valuing more than Rs. 100,000, track records of quotations were not being kept by the branch. Purchase Requisition file was also not maintained.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 'For Procurements valuing more than Rs. 100,000 a track of quotations received shall be maintained at Branch duly authenticated by PC to ensure that all quotations received are properly accounted for.' PR file must be maintained with copies of all PRs.
observations.audit_view: Track record of quotations above PKR 100,000 is essential for procurement transparency and auditability.
observations.typical_response: A proper filing system has now been implemented.

observations.title: Balance Confirmation Certificates not Obtained
observations.observation: Branch was unable to provide certain balance confirmation certificates from vendors/suppliers. A vendor (M/s Rang Studio) claimed Rs. 60,000 as receivable from the Branch while branch records show no amount payable.
observations.recommendation: For clarity of payables/receivables recorded in books of account, balance confirmation certificates should be obtained from all vendors at regular intervals. Discrepancies must be promptly investigated and reconciled.
observations.audit_view: The difference of Rs. 60,000 with M/S Rang Studio should be reconciled and books of account updated at the earliest. Balance confirmation should be obtained within specified time limits.
observations.typical_response: Most vendors ignore this request. Regarding M/s Rang Studio, as per our record no amount is payable.
